title: Operational runway sprint: burn checks + pricing guardrails
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet is a compact, actionable sprint checklist for finance + ops to run fast sensitivity scans on burn, headcount moves, and short-term pricing guardrails. Intended as a live artifact during the Q3 operational sprint (2-week cadence).

Executive summary:
- Quick objective: identify immediate headcount throttles and pricing levers that preserve >= 6 months runway under adverse scenarios without permanently harming GTM motion.
- Scope: token pricing bands, enterprise conversion lift, GPU spot-price shocks, and a pragmatic HC pause ladder.
- Outcome expected this sprint: a prioritized list of three reversible actions (1 pricing adjustment, 1 hiring pause, 1 infra/ops throttle) plus comms templates.

Scenario snapshot (high-level model outputs):
(Assumptions: current run-rate burn = $4.2M/mo, cash balance = $48M, base MRR = $6.5M, token mix steady-state)

| Scenario name               | Token price delta | Revenue delta (90d) | Runway (months) | HC freeze trigger           | Roles to pause first                | Recommended quick action                     |
|----------------------------|-------------------:|---------------------:|----------------:|-----------------------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| Base (status quo)          | 0%                | 0%                   | 11.4            | none                        | n/a                                  | No immediate action                            |
| Price compression -10%     | -10%              | -8%                  | 9.6             | MRR decline >7% over 30d    | New external hires (all teams)       | Temporary 8% token surcharge for non-SMB     |
| Enterprise uplift +20%     | +20%              | +15%                 | 12.8            | positive (monitor)          | n/a                                  | Accelerate Reserved capacity upsell program  |
| GPU spot spike x2 cost     | -                  | -6% (margin)         | 10.2            | GPU Opex >14% of monthly Opex| Infra hiring (infra/ops)             | Move non-critical clusters to burst pools    |

Notes on table: revenue delta uses cohort-weighted elasticity (see section below). Runway is cash / expected monthly net burn after scenario impacts.

Headcount throttle ladder (reversible, prioritized):
- Level 1 (soft): Pause external recruiting and contractor starts (impact: immediate -1.2M annualized).
- Level 2 (moderate): Hold non-customer-facing hiring (R&D research lab, new infra projects) (impact: -3.6M annualized).
- Level 3 (hard): Pause AEs ramp hires and delay 50% of planned CS hires (impact: -6.8M annualized).
- Level 4 (extreme): Selective short-term furlough for non-core projects; voluntary reduced hours program (impact: variable).

Concrete HC plan table (current planned hires vs trigger thresholds):

| Role                     | Planned hires (next 90d) | Trigger threshold to pause | Notes on re-hire sequencing                 |
|--------------------------|--------------------------:|---------------------------:|---------------------------------------------|
| Infra Engineers          | 8                        | GPU Opex > 12% or runway < 9m | Pause unless tied to reliability SLOs     |
| Serving Runtime Eng      | 6                        | MRR decline >5% over 60d    | Keep critical perf hires if quant savings >$X|
| SRE / Production         | 5                        | Error rate spike >1.5x      | Prioritize SRE for stability                |
| Sales AEs                | 7                        | Pipeline coverage < 0.6x    | Pause unless commit-backed deals exist      |
| Customer Success         | 4                        | Churn > 4% q/q              | Keep minimal coverage for top accounts     |

Pricing sensitivity by cohort (simplified):
- SMB (50% of tokens): price elasticity ~1.6 (sensitive).
- Mid-market (30%): elasticity ~0.8.
- Enterprise (20%): inelastic in short term, elasticity ~0.2 but large ACV impact.

Model: revenue_change = price_change * (1 - elasticity * uptake_factor)
Example: -10% price -> SMB revenue delta = -10% * (1 - 1.6) = +6% (i.e., risky; model flags increased usage but lower unit rev; we must cap by churn metric). Use capped elasticity for deep discounts.

Pricing guardrails (tactical options):
1) Temporary token surcharge for high-risk traffic (non-authenticated API paths) that can be removed with 72h notice.
2) Enterprise incentive: 12-week discounted reserved capacity vs immediate token rebate; aim to convert 8-10% of SMB token-hours to Reserved.
3) Auto-broker fallback: route low-priority batch jobs to cheaper pooled capacity during spot spikes; surfaced in console as a per-route opt-in.

Operational play checklist (two-week sprint):
- Finance: run a 5-scenario Monte Carlo with updated cohort mix (owner: Maya). Deadline: +4 business days.
- Product: prepare console toggle for temporary surcharge + Web UI copy (owner: Priya). Deadline: +6 business days.
- Infra: identify top-3 clusters for burst-to-spot migration; estimate customer impact (owner: Lucas). Deadline: +5 business days.
- GTM: draft external comms and partner play for enterprise upsell; prepare internal FAQ for sales (owner: Diego). Deadline: +7 business days.
- Legal: rapid review for surcharge wording and contract implications for customers with committed contracts (owner: Legal ops). Deadline: +3 business days.

Run assumptions (explicit):
- Current cash and burn numbers pulled from Finance ledger as of 2026-06-01.
- Elasticities are initial estimates based on historical small experiments (Jan–May 2026) and public comps; treat as priors rather than truths.
- GPU spot spike scenario assumes 40% of serving capacity is eligible for spot migration; rest is reserved.

Open questions / decision points: 
- Do we permit a token surcharge for trial/free accounts? (product + legal)
- IMMEDIATE threshold for hiring freeze: commit to Level 1 after X days of MRR decline — what is X? finance preference is 30d; GTM preference 45d.
- Contingency for multi-quarter price pressure: when to convert temporary surcharges into permanent price tiers?

Comms snippets (for execs):
- 1-line: "This sprint we propose reversible pricing and hiring levers to preserve runway while protecting our enterprise GTM."
- 2-line: "Proposed immediate actions: (1) pause non-critical external starts, (2) enable a temporary surcharge for uncommitted token traffic, (3) migrate non-critical clusters to burst pools until spot prices stabilize. These preserve ~1.8 months of runway in our -10% price case."

Appendix: quick numeric sensitivity (cells exported from modeling tool):
Base inputs: cash=$48,000,000; monthly burn=$4,200,000; base runway=11.4 months.
- Price compression -10%: incremental runway change = -1.8 months.
- Enterprise conversion +20%: runway +1.4 months if we capture 25% uplift in enterprise engagement.
- GPU spot x2: estimated margin hit leads to -1.2 months unless mitigated by burst moves.

Next steps (this sprint):
- Approve 3 reversible actions and commit owners/dates in the runbook.
- Finish Monte Carlo and attach exports to this doc (link back to GitHub sim).
- Schedule 30-minute cross-functional review on 2026-07-06.

Notes to reviewers: keep edits lightweight here — major model changes should be done in the simulation repo (linked above). This doc is the operational checklist and comms draft for the sprint.
